front_layout.gola_note: Verified from the p.39 elevation (zoomed 2026-08-16): undercounter recess above the top drawer; plain joint between the two 180 drawers; intermediate recess between the second drawer and the jumbo. Top drawer opens from the undercounter zone, second drawer from below via the intermediate zone, jumbo from above via the same zone. A gola drawer unit therefore needs BOTH profiles: undercounter (GOL001/GOL005) + intermediate (GOL002/GOL006), same system.

base_corner.description: Corner base unit - 1 rh or lh door, 8x8 fixed corner front panel, 1 shelf
base_corner.source_ref: printed p.42 / PDF 44; confirmed against printed p.10 (technical and dimensional information)
base_corner.notes: THE HAND IS PART OF THE CODE, AND IT IS NOT THE HINGE. The page prints every row as '...D/S' - Destra / Sinistra - and the letter names the EXECUTION of the cabinet: which end carries the door and the 8x8, and which end is blind with the wasted space behind it. S is the one drawn on the page (door at the left end, 8x8 immediately right of it); D is its mirror. A corner carcass is not symmetric, so the mirror cannot be had by turning the unit around - it is a different article, and both are needed in a U-shaped kitchen, one per corner. The 'LH' beside the drawing is something else entirely: it is the DOOR's hand, the ordinary per-order hinge_side, which does not change the code. Confirmed with Andriy 2026-08-17. Printed rules, verbatim: W.100/105 unit with 30 cm door - 90 cm carcass; W.115/120 unit with 45 cm door - 90 cm carcass; W.130/135 unit with 60 cm door - 120 cm carcass. The W notation is the space the corner NODE occupies, not the box: the second number is the unit's own depth + 80 (the 8x8 filler projecting forward), the first is the nominal length along the door wall. Nominal, in cm, with the 3 mm gaps not counted. Nominal minus the carcass length is WASTED SPACE - the unreachable depth of the corner, which must stay free and is drawn as edges only. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY on printed p.10 ('overall dimensions of corner base units', Technical and dimensional information), read 2026-08-17: the same three rules ('30-cm door for 95x65, 100x70, 105x75 base units, 90-cm carcass' and so on) plus a plan diagram. The diagram is labelled RH and shows the corner on the LEFT, the door at the RIGHT end, the 8x8 filler immediately left of the door, and the blind wasted zone further left behind the returning run - which is exactly our D execution mirrored from S. So RH (as drawn on p.10 and p.11) = D = destra = door at the right end. The engine's geometry matched the drawing with no change. CAUTION: p.10/p.11 draw the node RH while p.42 draws the same article LH - the hand can NEVER be read off a picture, only off the code letter (Elda Q7). p.10 also names a THIRD corner depth we do not hold: 95x65 / 110x65 / 125x65, i.e. d.57 (65 = 57 + 80). It is absent from p.42 and we have not found the page that prices it, so it is recorded as a gap, not guessed. p.10 further states when the 8x8 is mandatory: 'Fit corner base units with 8x8-cm fillers adjacent to drawer units, jumbo drawers and dishwashers (or custom-sized corner base units).'

front_layout.note: One door of 300/450/600 at the execution's end, then the 8x8 corner filler: ONE solid L, both legs 80 long and 22 thick, its front leg on the door plane and its return projecting forward so the perpendicular run meets it. The rest of the carcass front is blind. Door and filler share the front height, so door version 75 shortens both.
